slides.title: Book titles are special
slides.text:
The **title** is the name of a book.

When you write a book title in a sentence, you must **mark** it. Then readers know it is a title.

slides.title: Underline it
slides.text:
When you **write by hand**, draw a **line under** the book title.

I read The Lost Camel.

Draw a line under **The Lost Camel**.

slides.title: On a computer
slides.text:
When you **type**, you do not draw a line.

Use **italics** instead. Italics are slanted letters that lean to the right.

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
1. Read each sentence.
2. Find the **name of a book**.
3. That is the title. It must be underlined when you write by hand.

The sentence with the book's name is your proof.

sentences.t: My teacher read us The Brave Little Hawk.
The hawk in the story was very brave.

example.explain:
**The Brave Little Hawk** is the name of a book. By hand, we **underline** it.

In sentence 2, 'the hawk' is not a title. Nothing is underlined.

together.passage: I went to the library. I found a book called Sami and the Sea. It has big pictures. I took it home to read.
together.stem: You are writing by hand. What should you do with Sami and the Sea?
options: Write it all in small letters.
together.hint: Sami and the Sea is the name of a book. How do we mark a book title by hand?
together.good: Yes! It is a book title, so we draw a line under it.

sentences: I went to the library.
I found a book called Sami and the Sea.
It has big pictures.
I took it home to read.
evidence.stem: Tap the sentence that has a book title.
evidence.wrong: This sentence does not name a book. Find the name of a book.

checks.passage: Mona likes the book Stars at Night.
checks.stem: Which words are the book title?
checks.why: Stars at Night is the name of the book. That is the title.

checks.passage: We read Ten Green Frogs in class.
checks.stem: How do you mark the title when you write by hand?
checks.why: By hand, we draw a line under a book title.

checks.passage: Dad typed a list of books. One was The Big Dune.
checks.stem: How should The Big Dune look when it is typed?
options: with a dot after each word
checks.why: When we type a book title, we use italics instead of a line.

again.title: Is it the name of a book?
again.text:
Ask: **Is this the name of a book?**

Yes → underline it when you write by hand.

No → leave it plain.
again.example:
I read The Kind Camel. → book name → underline **The Kind Camel**.

I saw a kind camel. → not a book name → no line.

slides.title: Titles of books
slides.text:
The name of a **book** is a title. In a sentence, it must stand out.

By hand: **underline** it.
Typing: use **italics** (slanted letters).

slides.title: Underline the whole title
slides.text:
Underline **every word** of the title, even small words like **the**, **of** and **on**.

Right: a line under all of **The House on the Hill**
Wrong: a line under only **House** and **Hill**

slides.title: Only the title
slides.text:
Do not underline the word **book** or the author's name. Underline only the **title**.

I read the book Desert Stars by Nada Ali.

Underline only **Desert Stars**.

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
1. Find the words that name a **book**.
2. Check where the title starts and ends.
3. The whole title, and only the title, is underlined.

Point to the sentence that contains the book's title.

sentences.t: Our class is reading Journey to the Green Oasis.
The author, Huda Saleh, visited our school.

example.explain:
**Journey to the Green Oasis** is a book title. All of it is underlined, even **to** and **the**.

The author's name is not a title, so it is **not** underlined.

together.passage: Every Thursday, our class has a book club. This week, each student shared a favorite book. Bandar talked about The Secret of the Old Well. He said it was full of surprises. Next week, we will vote on a book to read together.
options: The Secret of the Old Well
together.hint: Only a title is underlined. Which words are the name of a book?
together.good: Yes! The Secret of the Old Well is the title of the book Bandar talked about.

sentences: Every Thursday, our class has a book club.
This week, each student shared a favorite book.
Bandar talked about The Secret of the Old Well.
He said it was full of surprises.
Next week, we will vote on a book to read together.
evidence.stem: Tap the sentence that contains a book title.
evidence.wrong: This sentence talks about books but does not name a title. Find the title.

checks.passage: Lina read the book Clouds Over Jeddah by Sara Omar.
options: Clouds Over Jeddah by Sara Omar
checks.why: Only the title is underlined, not the author's name.

checks.passage: The librarian typed the title of the new book on a card.
checks.stem: When a book title is typed, how should it look?
checks.why: A typed book title is put in italics, slanted letters.

checks.passage: Faris underlined only the word Ocean in the title The Deep Blue Ocean.
options: He should not underline the title.
He should underline the whole title.
checks.why: Every word of a title is underlined, from The to Ocean.

again.title: Find the edges
again.text:
A title has a **first word** and a **last word**.

Start your line under the first word. Stop under the last word. Every word in between gets the line too.
again.example:
We loved The Camel Who Could Not Sleep.

First word: **The**. Last word: **Sleep**. Underline all of **The Camel Who Could Not Sleep**.

slides.title: Long works
slides.text:
Titles of **long, whole works** are underlined (or in italics when typed):

• books
• plays
• newspapers and magazines
• movies

slides.title: Short works
slides.text:
Titles of **short works** go in **quotation marks**. They are often part of something bigger:

• poems
• short stories
• chapters
• articles

The poem "Morning in the Desert" is in a poetry book, and the book's title is underlined.

slides.title: Plays
slides.text:
A **play** is a story written to be acted on a stage. It is a whole work, so its title is **underlined**, like a book.

Our class performed The Clever Merchant.

Underline **The Clever Merchant**.

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
1. Find each title in the text.
2. Ask: Is it a **whole** long work (book, play, newspaper, movie) or a **short** part (poem, story, chapter, article)?
3. Whole work → underline. Short work → quotation marks.

Point to the sentence that tells you what kind of work the title names.

sentences.t: For the school festival, our class performed a play called The Honest Fisherman.
Before the play began, Reem read a poem titled "The Sea at Dawn."

example.explain:
**The Honest Fisherman** is a **play**, a whole work, so it is underlined.

**"The Sea at Dawn"** is a **poem**, a short work, so it goes in quotation marks.

together.passage: Our school held its yearly drama night on Wednesday. The older students performed a play called The Lantern Maker. It tells the story of a boy who brings light to his village. Before the show, the principal read a short article from the school newspaper. Many parents said it was the best drama night ever.
together.stem: How should The Lantern Maker be punctuated?
options: Put it in quotation marks, because it is short.
Underline it, because it is the title of a play.
Leave it plain, because it has capital letters.
Put commas around it, because it is a name.
together.hint: Find the clue word just before the title. What kind of work is it?
together.good: Yes! The text calls it a play. A play is a whole work, so its title is underlined.

sentences: Our school held its yearly drama night on Wednesday.
The older students performed a play called The Lantern Maker.
It tells the story of a boy who brings light to his village.
Before the show, the principal read a short article from the school newspaper.
Many parents said it was the best drama night ever.
evidence.stem: Tap the sentence that tells what kind of work The Lantern Maker is.
evidence.wrong: This sentence does not tell what kind of work the title names. Look for a clue word like play.

checks.passage: Nouf wrote a poem called Rain on the Roof for the school magazine.
checks.stem: How should the poem's title be punctuated?
checks.why: A poem is a short work, so its title goes in quotation marks.

checks.passage: The drama club is rehearsing a play titled The Lost Key.
checks.stem: Which is correct when writing by hand?
options: Put The Lost Key in quotation marks.
checks.why: The Lost Key is a play, a whole work, so the whole title is underlined.

checks.passage: In the novel Island of Palms, Chapter 4 is called The Storm.
checks.stem: Which title goes in quotation marks?
checks.why: The Storm is a chapter, a part of the book, so it goes in quotation marks. The novel's title is underlined.

again.title: Whole or part?
again.text:
Ask: **Can this work stand on its own, on a shelf or a stage?**

Yes (book, play, newspaper) → underline.

No, it is part of something bigger (poem, story, chapter, article) → quotation marks.
again.example:
The play The Wise Judge → acted on a stage by itself → **underline**.

The chapter "A New Friend" → part of a book → **quotation marks**.

slides.title: What underlining tells the reader
slides.text:
Underlining (or italics when typed) tells the reader: this is the title of a **complete, stand-alone work**.

Plays, books, newspapers, magazines and films are all stand-alone works.

A play's **acts** and **scenes** are parts, so words like Act 2 are not underlined.

slides.title: Choosing the right mark
slides.text:
Use the size of the work:

**Underline / italics**: plays, books, newspapers, magazines, films
**Quotation marks**: poems, short stories, chapters, articles

If a short work is inside a longer one, each gets its own mark: the article "Saving the Ibex" in the magazine Wild Arabia (underlined).

slides.title: What is not underlined
slides.text:
Some names are capitalized but are **not** underlined or put in quotation marks:

• the **Quran** and other sacred texts
• the author's or playwright's **name**
• words like **play**, **act** and **scene**

Underline only the exact title.

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
1. Find every title in the passage.
2. For each one, decide: a whole stand-alone work, or a part of a larger work?
3. Check the clue words around it: play, performed, act, scene, poem, chapter, article.
4. Match the mark to the kind of work.

Point to the sentences whose clue words prove what kind of work a title names.

sentences.t: The writer Majid Saad wrote The Pearl Divers many years ago.
The play was first performed in Jeddah, and its second act is the most famous.
In that act, the main character recites a poem called "The Gulf at Night."

example.explain:
Sentence 2 shows that **The Pearl Divers** is a **play**, so its title is underlined. The act is part of the play, so it is not.

The **poem** is a short work inside the play, so its title goes in quotation marks.

together.passage: For our class project, we compared two versions of the same old tale. The first was a book called The Merchant and the Falcon. The second was a play based on the book, which the city theater performed last spring. The play was titled The Falcon's Return. In Act 1, a character reads aloud a short poem, "Wings Over the Dunes." Our class decided that the play brought the story to life in a new way.
together.stem: Which title should be underlined because it names a play?
together.hint: The book is underlined too, but it is not a play. Find the title that the text calls a play.
together.good: Yes! The text says the play was titled The Falcon's Return. A play is a whole work, so it is underlined.

sentences: For our class project, we compared two versions of the same old tale.
The first was a book called The Merchant and the Falcon.
The second was a play based on the book, which the city theater performed last spring.
The play was titled The Falcon's Return.
In Act 1, a character reads aloud a short poem, "Wings Over the Dunes."
Our class decided that the play brought the story to life in a new way.
evidence.stem: Tap 2 sentences that prove The Falcon's Return is a play.
evidence.wrong: This sentence names a different kind of work, or does not give a title. Look for the clue word play.

checks.passage: Last night, I watched a performance of The Tent of Stories at the cultural center.
checks.stem: Why should The Tent of Stories be underlined?
options: It is the title of a play, a whole work.
It is the name of a building.
It is the title of a short poem.
It begins with the word The.
checks.why: It was performed, so it is a play. Plays are whole works, so their titles are underlined.

checks.passage: Scene 3 of the play The Generous Neighbor takes place in a busy market.
checks.why: Only the play's title is underlined. A scene is a part of the play, so Scene 3 is not.

checks.passage: Our teacher read us the article Why Bees Matter from the magazine Desert Explorer.
checks.stem: How should the two titles be punctuated?
options: Article underlined; magazine in quotation marks
Article in quotation marks; magazine underlined
checks.why: An article is a short part of a magazine, so it gets quotation marks. The magazine is a whole work, so it is underlined.

again.title: Stage, shelf or page?
again.text:
Ask where the work lives.

**On a stage** (play) or **on a shelf** (book, magazine) → underline.

**On a page inside something bigger** (poem, chapter, article) → quotation marks.
again.example:
The Two Brothers was performed at the theater. → on a stage → **underline The Two Brothers**.

Its opening poem, "Home," → a page inside the play → **quotation marks**.
